## What it is

- The **Hammond B-3** and **C-3** came out in **1954**, with harmonic percussion, and were made until early **1975** (Wikipedia, "Hammond organ"). The C-3 is the same organ in a closed church-style cabinet (UNVERIFIED detail).
- It is *electromechanical*: spinning **tonewheels** past pickups make the pitches, close to pure sine waves.
- Two manuals of 61 keys and a pedalboard (Wikipedia).
- It is usually played through a **Leslie speaker** such as the 122, which spins a horn and a drum (Wikipedia, "Hammond organ").

## Its sound

- **Drawbars** mix nine pitches of every key, from 16′ (an octave below) to 1′ (three octaves above). Pull one out to make it louder.
- **Preset keys**: the reverse-coloured octave to the left. C silences the manual, A♯ and B pick the two drawbar sets, the others are presets (Wikipedia).
- **Percussion** adds a quick 2nd or 3rd harmonic to the start of a note; only on the upper manual with preset B, and it silences the 1′ drawbar (Hammond XK-5 manual, "same as B-3/C-3").
- **Vibrato and chorus**: six settings V1 V2 V3 C1 C2 C3, on or off for each manual (Wikipedia).
- **Leslie**: slow (chorale) or fast (tremolo). The horn speeds up faster than the drum.

## Guided tour

Each step loads a registration and plays the same short phrase: chords on the lower manual, a tune on the upper, a bass line on the pedals.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="b3-flute"><p><b>A preset.</b> Preset key <b>C♯</b>, <i>Stopped Flute</i> (00 5320 000). Listen: soft and hollow.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="b3-jazz" data-set="{&quot;perc&quot;:false,&quot;leslie&quot;:&quot;stop&quot;,&quot;vibU&quot;:false}"><p><b>Three drawbars.</b> Preset <b>B</b>, drawbars 88 8000 000, nothing else. Listen: a round, plain organ tone.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="b3-jazz" data-set="{&quot;leslie&quot;:&quot;stop&quot;,&quot;vibU&quot;:false}"><p><b>Percussion.</b> Add <b>3rd harmonic, soft, fast</b> percussion. Listen for a click of pitch at the start of each melody note.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="b3-jazz" data-set="{&quot;leslie&quot;:&quot;stop&quot;}"><p><b>Chorus C3.</b> Turn the scanner on for the upper manual on <b>C3</b>. Listen: a shimmer around each note.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="b3-jazz"><p><b>Leslie slow.</b> The same with the Leslie on <b>chorale</b>. Listen: the sound moves round the room.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="b3-full"><p><b>Everything out, Leslie fast.</b> All nine drawbars at 8 and the Leslie on <b>tremolo</b>, with some drive. Listen: loud, bright and spinning.</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Hammond organ":

- Booker T. & the M.G.'s, "Green Onions"
- Procol Harum, "A Whiter Shade of Pale" (Matthew Fisher)
- The Spencer Davis Group, "Gimme Some Lovin'" (Steve Winwood)
- Jimmy Smith, "Walk on the Wild Side"

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What makes the B-3&#x27;s pitches?</b></p><ul><li>Spinning tonewheels</li><li>Pipes and wind</li><li>A tape loop</li><li>Twelve transistor oscillators</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Tonewheels past pickups.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>You pull a drawbar further out. What happens?</b></p><ul><li>Its pitch gets louder</li><li>It goes up an octave</li><li>The Leslie speeds up</li><li>Nothing</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Out = louder.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Which preset key cancels the manual?</b></p><ul><li>C</li><li>B</li><li>A♯</li><li>F</li></ul><p class="ik-why">C is the cancel key (Wikipedia).</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Percussion works…</b></p><ul><li>On the upper manual with preset B</li><li>On the pedals</li><li>On every preset</li><li>Only with the Leslie fast</li></ul><p class="ik-why">XK-5 manual, as on the B-3.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Leslie &#x27;tremolo&#x27; is…</b></p><ul><li>The fast speed</li><li>The slow speed</li><li>Stopped</li><li>A reverb</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Chorale slow, tremolo fast.</p></div>
```

An emulator's table of the B-3 factory presets; upper C-sharp to E agree with a second web page. Not a Hammond document: the other presets are unverified.

Hammond Suzuki. "XK-5 Owner's Manual." *ManualsLib*. [www.manualslib.com/manual/1591989/Hammond-Xk-5.html?page=52](https://www.manualslib.com/manual/1591989/Hammond-Xk-5.html?page=52). Percussion: 2nd = the 4′ drawbar's pitch, 3rd = the 2⅔′; fast / slow decay; the 1′ drawbar inoperative while on; only with the B preset key and only on the upper manual, 'same as B-3/C-3'. Read as quoted in a search result, page not opened in full.

**For students**

"Hammond organ." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammond_organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammond_organ). B-3 / C-3 1954 to early 1975, harmonic percussion; 61-key manuals, 25-note pedalboard; reverse-coloured preset keys, C cancel, B and B-flat the drawbar sets; percussion 2nd / 3rd, soft / normal, single-trigger; V1-V3 C1-C3 per manual; Leslie 122; players and records.
